hero.headline: I turn complex systems into
hero.lede: I’m Felipe Hamasaki, a full stack developer in Brazil. I turn complex intelligence, tracking, and fraud-prevention workflows into clear, dependable products.

work.title: Proof, not promises.
work.intro: Production systems are private. These concise case studies explain the problem, my contribution, and the result without presenting confidential work as a public demo.

one.title: Intelligence platform for 24/7 operations
one.problem: Analysts need to connect live vehicle tracking, mapping, advanced search, and sensitive records without losing context.
one.solution: I build and modernise React and Next.js interfaces while extending Node.js, Express, and MySQL services behind them.

two.title: Real-time telecom site monitoring
two.problem: Security teams need one live view of remote tower sites and the hardware protecting them.
two.solution: I helped build video, smoke, access, and anti-theft monitoring using WebSocket and polling, integrated with in-house hardware.

three.title: A component library shared across products
three.problem: Product interfaces were repeating the same decisions and drifting as the platform grew.
three.solution: I built and maintained a private React package and introduced shared tooling, naming, release, and documentation conventions.

stack.title: Right tool. Clear reason.
stack.intro: Technologies I use in production, grouped by the job they do — without arbitrary percentage bars.

about.paragraph1: I’m a full stack developer based in São Paulo state. I build and modernise operational software for corporate intelligence and fraud prevention, where reliability matters because people use the product all day.
about.paragraph2: I started on the frontend and now work across the stack. I like being close to product decisions, making trade-offs explicit, and improving the conventions that help a small team move together.
about.paragraph3: Before software, I taught English for two years and spent six years in HR. Payroll taught me that some bugs are personal; the classroom taught me to explain complicated things without hiding behind jargon.

fullstack.impact: Building intelligence and fraud-prevention products used around the clock by approximately 100 analysts.

frontend.impact: Built and maintained a private package of approximately 50 React components and introduced conventions adopted by a five-developer team.

junior.impact: Built responsive operator interfaces with React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.

hrAnalyst.impact: Ran payroll, time-and-attendance systems, onboarding, offboarding, and management reporting for an American manufacturer.

hrIntern.impact: Supported personnel administration and built reporting and data cross-referencing in Excel.

teacher.impact: Taught beginner-to-intermediate English for two years.

About.title: About
About.intro: I build and modernise operational software for corporate intelligence and fraud prevention. I got here through human resources and an English classroom, which matters more than it may sound.
About.story1: I grew up around computers, largely because my father was a web designer and journalist. I was always drawn to games and PCs, but it took time to see software as work rather than only a hobby.
About.story2: I taught English for two years, then spent six years in human resources at an American automotive multinational. I started as an intern and became a personnel administration analyst, working with payroll, time-and-attendance systems, onboarding, offboarding, and management reporting.
About.story3: The part of that job I enjoyed most was building reports. I spent years cross-referencing data in Excel, understanding what a number meant, and presenting it so someone else could act on it. In 2020 I began studying Python and JavaScript in the evenings with the specific goal of changing careers.
About.story4: I joined ODEEN in January 2022 as a junior frontend developer. I progressed to frontend developer and then to full stack developer, working with React and Next.js on the interface and Node.js, Express, and MySQL behind it. I completed a degree in Systems Analysis and Development while working full-time.
About.story5: The HR years are the least obvious part of my CV and the part I would defend hardest. Six years of payroll teaches you that some mistakes are not recoverable, that the person facing a bad interface is having a worse day than its developer, and that documentation only works when it is easy to use. I build operator tools now. It is the same responsibility with different inputs.
About.photoCaption: Around the time computers became interesting.
About.work1: I care about conventions more than most people find reasonable. On my current team I helped move linting from ESLint to Biome, standardised pnpm, and introduced release-based branching plus naming and documentation rules. These changes were not assigned to me, and they were adopted after discussion with the team.
About.work2: I like being involved when technical decisions are made, making alternatives and costs explicit, and then supporting the decision the team takes.
About.work3: I use AI tooling heavily and I am direct about it. It has changed how much I can take on, but I still treat the output as something I am responsible for understanding and reviewing.
About.work4: English has been part of my professional life since before software: I taught it for two years, used it with a US organisation in the automotive industry, and earned an EF SET C2 certificate in reading and listening.
About.skillsIntro: Grouped by how deeply I actually use them, not by how many I can name.
About.contextNote: Platform context means exactly that: the systems I work on use these technologies and controls, but infrastructure, delivery pipelines, and authentication are owned by other people on the team.
